# Becker-Coppens measured-data reference

`generate_extinction_fit.py` is an authoring tool; tests only read its frozen output.
It imports NumPy and SciPy, never Crysta, Edi, diffraction-lib or CrysPy.

The unextincted F² basis comes from the committed FullProf 8.40 basic Tb₂Ti₂O₇
OUT, divided by its PCR scale 3.653. That basic structure and the extinction
project structure are byte-identical; the generator checks this and the reflection
order before fitting. The measured INT observations, uncertainties, wavelength
0.793 Å and cubic cell 10.130 Å retain the source PCR precision and occupancies.
Input hashes and upstream revision are in `reference.json`.

The primary and Gaussian secondary factors are the spherical Becker–Coppens
approximations, Becker & Coppens, Acta Cryst. A30 (1974), 129–147,
https://doi.org/10.1107/S0567739474000337. They are the same independently
transcribed equations as `../../generate_projects.py` and `../../extinction.json`.
Radius is in μm; stored mosaicity uses the upstream numerical factor pi/10800
and is held at 35000, without claiming it is an angle. Extinction acts on the
unscaled F² before the fitted scale. FullProf's empirical Ext1 is never used.

SciPy least_squares fits scale and radius from (4.1744, 10), with nonnegative
bounds and a three-point Jacobian. All 220 observations participate. The
objective is sum(r²)/(220−2). Parameter s.u.s are the square roots of the
diagonal of inv(JᵀJ) times that reduced objective; the frozen record also
contains the correlation and the column-normalized Jacobian condition.
This describes the fixed-mosaicity fit, not a radius/mosaicity joint fit.

The basis is printed to four decimals, so its absolute rounding is at most
0.00005/3.653 before extinction. Expected scale and radius bounds are one
independent s.u. each. The objective retains the earlier gate's 0.06 absolute
and 0.2% relative bounds; no bound was fitted to product output. The original
FullProf empirical-extinction fitting twin is retained under `../fullprof`
as a diagnostic of a different model, not as the Becker–Coppens oracle.

Reproduce from the repository root with:

```sh
python tests/fixtures/single_crystal/generate_extinction_fit.py
```

The committed result is scale 3.6799768101945864 ± 0.10288873814942545,
radius 16.550771124907907 ± 2.225559273639577 μm and reduced χ²
76.79365259985084. Provenance: the companion reference.json, generated by the
command above; no product output supplies any of these values.
